DISCUSSION
A DC Compound motor consists of a Shunt Field coil and a Series Field coil.
The combination of the Series and Shunt field coils provides the magnetic field for the armature.
The compound motor represents a compromise between the characteristics of Series and Shunt motors.

The Series motor exhibits a higher starting torque than the Shunt motor.
On the other hand, the Shunt motor exhibits higher torque at higher RPM.
The Compound Motor's start and run torque is between the high and low torque of the Series and Shunt Motors.
The Compound Motor has lower starting torque but higher running torque than the Series Motor.
The Compound Motor has higher starting and lower running torque than the Shunt Motor.

The Compound motor incorporates simultaneous Shunt and Series field connections.
There are two possible ways to configure a DC Compound motor.
The Long Shunt Compound motor has the shunt coil connected across the series coil and armature.
In this type of Compound motor, the Armature Current (I ) and the Series Field current (I ) are the same.
The shunt coil voltage is the same as the sum of the armature voltage and the series coil voltage, or the applied voltage.
The Short Shunt Compound motor has a coil in series with the Armature (series coil) and a coil connected in parallel with the armature only (Shunt coil).
In this type of Compound motor, the Series Coil Current (I ) is the sum of the Shunt Coil Current (I ) and the Armature Current (I ).
The shunt coil voltage (V ) is the same as the armature coil voltage (V ).
As with all DC motors, locked rotor torque is the product of the armature current, field current and the constant.
In a Compound motor, I is a function of both the Series (SER) and Shunt (SH) fields.
Because a Compound motor utilizes both field coils, each coil contributes to flux generation in the armature.
Maximum motor performance occurs when the coil fields are additive.
